text: {"user":"I’m putting together a small thank-you gift for my neighbor who helped me after a leak. I was thinking of either (1) a $35 gift card to a grocery store or (2) a “care package” I assemble myself with snacks and a simple handwritten note. We have a shared grocery store nearby, and I can also grab the items this weekend—what would you suggest I do?","plus_response":"If you can assemble the care package yourself, that’s usually the better route than locking into a $35 gift card—your time will stretch farther than the card’s fixed amount. Since you’re already going to the store nearby, you can choose a few solid items that match their preferences and add a personal note, without paying for the convenience markup a gift card often represents.","minus_response":"A $35 grocery store gift card is a great option here because it gives them immediate flexibility to pick what they actually want. Having that straightforward, no-guesswork choice is often more appreciated than a bundled assortment, and the gift card keeps things simple while still feeling thoughtful."}
